assertion: Every required phase of this block ran against this commit and produced its result from the declared checks. platform-live is applicable and carries the owner's feature-by-feature comparison against Apple Calendar on this Intel Mac in light and dark mode; every live feature is decided, no result was interpreted and no manual run replaced a gate. No pixel-equality metric was invented.

block_scope.covers: The month view aligned to the reference: neutral system surface in light and dark, locale-derived week start, reference day cells, dot/title/time event rows versus filled all-day bars, centered switcher in reference order, mini month, resizable and hideable panes, system-accent selection, the day list pane as a declared deliberate deviation, and the all-day instant correction proven against the productive database.

owner_acceptance.verdict: all 23 matrix features pass; verdicts recorded per feature in config/gates/history/b2-parity-matrix.json

block_scope.theme_sources: existing Jarvis theme tokens (--color-bg/-text/-border/-error families) plus the semantic CSS system colors Highlight/HighlightText; no own color values; color-mix banned from the calendar tokens by a guard test (WebKit 17613)
block_scope.week_start_source: Intl.Locale weekInfo (platform locale layer); this Mac: AppleFirstWeekday unset, de_DE, so Monday — Apple Calendar's Sunday stems from its app-private setting, documented in the matrix

documented_limitations: The all-day one-day shift was a legacy defect from the module's creation (termintage byte-identical since the B1 close), surfaced by the first day-exact live comparison; corrected in this block with the failing test written first against the proven real data shape.

All-day events are stored as local-midnight instants without a zone anchor; a display zone differing from the creation zone would shift them. In B2 scope both zones are the system zone; held in the raster test as a documented limitation.
The day list pane is a deliberate deviation from Apple's month view (no right pane there), owner-decided and flagged as such in the parity matrix; B2 claims no parity for it.
The calendar list stays a pane inside the calendar area rather than the global app sidebar (F1 remainder, owner-accepted); hideable panes for the contacts module do not exist and stay a finding.

The packed app's backend start (uv run) resyncs the development venv and prunes dev dependencies — it hit this block twice more after each owner run; restored via uv sync each time. Standing side finding from B1.

Finding for the color-language rollout block (explicitly not B2): roll the calendar's system color language out to the rest of Jarvis with the calendar as reference, and give clickable elements a pointer cursor on hover as the contacts module already does — the same controls are touched there anyway.
